meta.title: Little Red-Cap
meta.author: The Brothers Grimm
meta.blurb: Take the cake and wine to grandmother, says her mother, and don't stray from the path. But the wood is full of flowers, and someone friendly asks where she is going.

chapters.title: Little Red-Cap. By the Brothers Grimm.

segments.speaker: host
segments.text: A girl, a basket, a wood, and a wolf. Perhaps the most retold story in the world.
phrases: A girl, a basket, a wood, and a wolf.
Perhaps the most retold story in the world.

segments.speaker: host
segments.text: Charles Perrault wrote it down in France in sixteen ninety-seven, and his version ends with the wolf's dinner. When the Brothers Grimm heard it in Hesse, a hundred years later, the tellers had given it a huntsman, and a second chance.
phrases: Charles Perrault wrote it down in France in sixteen ninety-seven, and his version ends with the wolf's dinner.
When the Brothers Grimm heard it in Hesse, a hundred years later, the tellers had given it a huntsman, and a second chance.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Once upon a time there was a dear little girl who was loved by everyone who looked at her, but most of all by her grandmother, and there was nothing that she would not have given to the child. Once she gave her a little cap of red velvet, which suited her so well that she would never wear anything else; so she was always called
